title: Degree Bounds for Identification Formulas in Linear Gaussian Mixed Graphs
banked_reason: The advertised sharp identifying-degree frontier is not determined: only a loose effective Gröbner cutoff was proved, while the matching lower family and bounded-versus-unbounded elbow remain open.
gap_reasons: The proposal's sharp full-class indegree-two frontier (matching upper and lower bounds) is still explicitly unresolved; the delivered effective Dubé cutoff is a materially weaker object and must be repositioned as such rather than presented as fulfillment of that frontier promise.

The advertised sharp identifying-degree frontier is not determined: the note proves only the very loose bracket 3 <= D2(n) <= U2(n), where U2 is a generic double-exponential Gröbner bound rather than an intrinsic rate.
After the windmill family failed, no admissible lower family remains.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery tested the proposed windmill lower family, rejected it by a parameter-dimension obstruction, and derived a valid graph-sensitive Dubé elimination bound, an unconditional stopping schedule, and a rational K6 inverse of degree at most seven. The sharp-frontier kernel nevertheless collapsed because neither the exact K6 lower certificate nor a dimension-feasible substitution-robust asymptotic lower family was established. Determining whether D2(n) is bounded, and matching that answer with an intrinsic upper bound, remains open.
tldr: For every rationally identifiable acyclic linear Gaussian mixed graph, eliminating the supported disturbance covariances first leaves missing-bidirected cubic equations in \(n(n+1)/2+|D|\) variables and gives the graph-sensitive bound \(ID_G\leq\mathfrak B(G)=\lfloor2(15/2)^{2^{n(n+1)/2+|D|-1}}\rfloor\). Structural coefficients have direct certificates at this cutoff, and all disturbance coordinates follow by recursive degree-three certificates. This yields a graph-sensitive total exact call to the degree-bounded identification algorithm. For directed indegree at most two, \(|D|\leq2n-3\) sharpens the graph-independent cutoff to \(U_2(1)=15\) and \(U_2(n)=\lfloor2(15/2)^{2^{n(n+1)/2+2n-4}}\rfloor\) for \(n\geq2\). The exact value of \(ID_{K_6}\) and the bounded-versus-unbounded elbow for \(D_2(n)\) remain open.
gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's algorithm is complete only relative to a supplied degree. Their Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 give \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses, and Proposition 7.4 gives \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for auxiliary cutsets, specializing to \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\). No theorem calibrates minimum recursive degree over all rationally identifiable indegree-two graphs or exhibits an explicit family outside auxiliary cutsets with an order-robust lower invariant.
fill: The central open-ended question proves matching bounds for \(D_2(n)\), establishes the padded two-parent windmills as a rationally identifiable family outside all three bounded graphical subclasses, and lower-bounds them with \(\mathfrak H_{\ell,d}(S)\) over every degree-reachable predecessor set. The mandatory \(W_3^{(2)}\) audit supplies coordinate formulas, three complete criterion-failure transcripts, and every degree-four obstruction matrix before the family induction. The resulting cutoff is compiled conditionally into exact formula output and total finite-sample fixed-chart inference.
